subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should OpenClaw keep fenced `MEDIA:` directives as text with a warn-once delivery-boundary diagnostic, extract fenced directives as attachments, or document the behavior as by design?
rationale: The parser currently protects code examples from mutation, and the linked PR discussion shows multiple viable contracts with different delivery and transcript risks.

options.title: Warn once at delivery boundary
options.body: Keep fenced examples as text and add a single operator-visible warning only when final outbound delivery would otherwise silently skip a fenced legacy media directive.

options.title: Extract fenced directives
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting the risk that code examples can turn into media sends.

options.title: Docs-only by design
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on documentation to tell users that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn once at delivery boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced examples as text and add a single operator-visible warning only when final outbound delivery would otherwise silently skip a fenced legacy media directive.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest review on the linked PR gives the most concrete maintainer direction for where the warning should live.
